name: Shimei
overview: Shimei was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified uniquely as the son of Pedaiah. His lineage is noted in 1 Chronicles 3:19, situating him within the genealogical records of the tribe. There are no additional notes expanding on his life or character beyond this genealogical mention.
namesAndTitles: The name Shimei means 'YHWH has heard' or 'famous,' reflecting a Hebrew origin that emphasizes God's attentiveness or renown. This proper name was not given directly by God but carries a meaningful theophoric element common in biblical names.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Shimei as the son of Pedaiah, as stated in 1 Chronicles 3:19, and also as the son of Ela, according to 1 Kings 4:18. These explicit relationships place him within the family lines of Judah, though no further family details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: Shimei's significance lies primarily in his place within the genealogical framework of Judah, which is important for understanding the lineage and tribal heritage of Israel. His mention in Scripture contributes to the historical and theological continuity of God's covenant people. While not prominent in narrative events, his inclusion underscores the biblical emphasis on family lines and God's providence in history.
